metadata.domain: AI Vision Perception / ADAS / Computer Vision

evidence.trl_pathway: Chiplet-Based AI Accelerators (TRL 3) is scheduled to complete in just 1 quarter (2027-Q1 to Q2), which is wholly unrealistic for a TRL 3 architecture technology; similarly, advancing HBM Integration from TRL 4 to deployment-ready in 5 quarters is aggressive, and both are compounded by confirmed dependency violations where prerequisites haven't yet completed.
evidence.strategic_fidelity: The portfolio includes some lower-TRL exploratory technologies (Neuromorphic TRL 2, Chiplet TRL 3) consistent with 기술선도, but also high-TRL process technologies like ISO 26262 certification (TRL 7) and AI Model Compression (TRL 6) that are near-commercial rather than leadership-oriented, creating mixed strategic signals.
evidence.competitive_awareness: HBM Integration and Advanced Packaging for AI are memory/semiconductor packaging technologies that fall significantly outside the stated AI Vision Perception/ADAS/Computer Vision domain — an ADAS-focused company would face severe competitive disadvantage against established semiconductor giants in these areas, indicating weak domain fit and competitive positioning.
evidence.market_timing: Five of seven technologies hit their boom windows exactly (0.0yr error), which aligns well with 시장이익최대 logic but is only moderately aligned with 기술선도 which should ideally complete 1-2 years before boom; Event-Based Vision Processing and Neuromorphic Computing complete 0.75 years after their respective booms, missing even the market-profit window.
evidence.patent_market_convergence: The selection of technologies like Event-Based Vision Processing and Neuromorphic Computing suggests some awareness of emerging patent-active domains, but the inclusion of mature process technologies (ISO 26262, AI Model Compression) and the hardware packaging stack suggests the selection was driven more by supply-chain completeness than deliberate patent-market convergence analysis.

strengths: Five technologies achieve near-perfect boom timing alignment (0.0yr error), demonstrating strong timeline execution discipline for those items.
Neuromorphic Computing (TRL 2) and Event-Based Vision Processing (TRL 4) are genuinely exploratory selections appropriate for a technology leadership posture in the vision perception domain.
weaknesses: Two confirmed dependency violations (Chiplet-Based AI Accelerators and HBM Integration both start before their S03 prerequisite completes), making those development paths structurally infeasible as planned.

HBM Integration and Advanced Packaging for AI are semiconductor hardware/packaging technologies far outside the AI Vision Perception/ADAS domain, where the company has no established competitive advantage.
missing_technologies: 3D Object Detection / Point Cloud Fusion (core ADAS perception stack)
Transformer-based Vision Foundation Models for autonomous driving
Federated Learning for in-vehicle perception model updates
investment_issues: All 7 technologies are assigned Tier=High with identical scores across all dimensions, suggesting a lack of genuine portfolio differentiation and priority-setting — a uniform high-tier allocation is not a real investment strategy.

High investment in HBM Integration and Advanced Packaging (hardware infrastructure plays) diverts resources from core ADAS/computer vision algorithm and software technologies where the company would have stronger competitive leverage.
timing_issues: Chiplet-Based AI Accelerators (TRL 3) allocated only 1 quarter of development time — advancing from early prototype to completion in one quarter is industrially infeasible.
Event-Based Vision Processing completes 0.75 years after its market boom (2029-Q1), missing the optimal window for both leadership and profit strategies.

Neuromorphic Computing completes 0.75 years after its 2030-Q1 boom, and for a 기술선도 strategy it should ideally complete 1-2 years before boom, meaning it is actually 1.75-2.75 years late relative to the leadership ideal.
